home.hero.lead: A lean, privacy-friendly PDF reader for everyday work: read, annotate, sign and organize. Everything runs locally in your browser — no backend, no telemetry.
home.usp.heading: Three features Acrobat doesn't have
home.usp.signature.title: Signature with hash integrity
home.usp.signature.body: Place a PNG signature, write signer details into the PDF info dictionary — and a SHA-256 hash over content + annotations turns the status badge red the moment anything is changed afterwards.
home.usp.library.title: Library with sidecar
home.usp.library.body: Every PDF you open lands in the library automatically — with SHA-256 identity, tags and inline filter. Annotations export to a JSON sidecar next to the PDF and re-import on a different device.
home.usp.markdown.title: Markdown export
home.usp.markdown.body: Dump highlights and notes as Markdown with YAML frontmatter, wikilinks and per-page grouping — straight into your Obsidian vault or Zettelkasten of choice.
home.builtin.heading: Features
home.builtin.viewer: Open PDFs, page navigation, zoom, full-text search, outline sidebar
home.builtin.annotations: Highlights in 5 colors, sticky notes with live markdown preview, pen + rectangle/arrow/line
home.builtin.signature: Place PNG signature, drag/resize, signer data, save signed PDF
home.builtin.tools: Rotate, delete, reorder pages, merge, split, JPEG compress
home.builtin.ocr: OCR via Tesseract.js for non-searchable PDFs (scans, designer layouts)
home.builtin.viewerExtras: Thumbnail sidebar, split view for two PDFs, theme switcher, DE/EN
home.margin.heading: At a glance
home.colophon.heading: Privacy
home.privacy.title: Fully local
home.privacy.body: No backend, no cookies, no accounts, no telemetry and no external requests. OCR runs fully locally too (Tesseract.js, self-hosted) — nothing is fetched from a CDN.

tools.pdfa.label: PDF/A (best effort):
tools.pdfa.buttonTitle: Prepare the PDF towards PDF/A-2b (XMP, sRGB output intent, cleanup) and download — no conformance guarantee
tools.pdfa.note: Best-effort approximation of PDF/A-2b: XMP identification, sRGB output intent, removal of JavaScript and auto actions. Non-embedded standard fonts (Helvetica/Times/Courier) can be replaced with metrically compatible, embedded Liberation fonts (SIL OFL 1.1); other fonts are only reported, not repaired — no conformance guarantee. For archival use, verify the result externally (e.g. with veraPDF).
tools.pdfa.embedFontsTitle: Replace non-embedded standard-14 fonts (Helvetica/Times/Courier) with metrically compatible, embedded Liberation fonts (SIL OFL 1.1); Symbol/ZapfDingbats are not replaced
tools.pdfua.label: PDF/UA (identification + report):
tools.pdfua.buttonTitle: Set the PDF/UA identification (MarkInfo, document language, DisplayDocTitle, XMP pdfuaid:part=1), create a report and download as -ua.pdf — no conformance guarantee
tools.pdfua.note: Best effort: only sets the PDF/UA identification (MarkInfo, document language, DisplayDocTitle, XMP pdfuaid:part=1) and honestly reports what is missing — tagging, document title, alternative texts, ToUnicode. Real tagging (structure tree, reading order) cannot be synthesized — no conformance guarantee. For a binding check, use external tools (e.g. veraPDF or PAC).
tools.sign.label: Sign (certificate, P12):
tools.sign.buttonTitle: Sign the loaded PDF with the certificate (adbe.pkcs7.detached, SHA-256) and download as -signiert.pdf
tools.sign.note: Classic certificate-based PDF signature (adbe.pkcs7.detached, SHA-256, CMS with signed attributes, certificate chain embedded) — verifiable in Adobe/Foxit. Password and certificate never leave your browser. Honest limits: no timestamp server (PAdES-B-T) and no LTV — the app works offline; the signingCertificateV2 attribute is omitted. Already-signed PDFs are rejected. Not to be confused with the image signature with hash badge in the reader: that is a visual signature, this creates a cryptographic one.
tools.convert.title: Convert the loaded PDF to the selected format and download
tools.convert.note: PNG/JPG produce a ZIP with one image per page; HTML embeds each page as an image (pixel-accurate, opens offline). DOCX is a best-effort text flow (paragraphs are reconstructed, no 1:1 layout fidelity — choose HTML/PNG for pixel fidelity); XLSX uses the table heuristic (one sheet per page); PPTX creates one slide per page with the page image. SVG produces editable vector (paths + text with the original fonts embedded); pages with gradients or non-extractable images fall back to an embedded raster — one SVG per page inside a ZIP. The originally loaded PDF is converted.
